disclaimers.aiPlans: AI helps draft plans and pick swaps — and it can get things wrong. Review every plan, recipe and swap against your own dietary needs and health before you rely on it.
disclaimers.enginePlans: Plan generation and swaps run on a deterministic engine — fast and reproducible, but still review every result against your own dietary needs and health. After an ingredient swap the recipe text is adjusted by plain replacement: it may read awkwardly, and a step that names the old ingredient by another word still names it. The ingredient list is the one to follow.
disclaimers.aiRecipeDraft: AI-drafted recipes can contain mistakes. Double-check the ingredients, quantities and steps before relying on the result.
disclaimers.aiActivated: AI helps draft recipes and pick swaps, but it can make mistakes. Always review AI-generated content against your own dietary needs and health.
disclaimers.bugReport: Spotted a bug? <link>Open an issue</link> on the source repository.

devWarning.title: Heads up — early development.
devWarning.body: This is pre-release software under active development. Things may break, data may be wiped between updates, and it might just blow up in your face. Don't rely on it for anything important yet.

landing.headline: Meal planning that actually adds up.
landing.subhead: Calorie-targeted plans, deterministic nutrition and shopping lists that write themselves. AI optional — never required.

features.nutritionBody: Every calorie and macro comes from a curated database — reproducible, never invented.

features.listsBody: Shopping lists merged, unit-normalised and grouped by aisle.
features.aiBody: Bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter or Ollama key. Works fully without one.

admin.title: Diet App · Admin
admin.subhead: Instance-only stats — no user data is shown.
admin.restartHint: Restart the API container after editing .env so the new value is picked up.
admin.credsHint: You sign in once: the browser keeps a session for eight hours and no password.
admin.endAllSessionsHint: Signs out every browser that is signed in to this panel, this one too.
admin.invalidCredsOrCode: User, password or code is wrong. Try again.
admin.secondFactorBody: With it, signing in to the panel takes a code from an authenticator app as well as the password.
admin.secondFactorOn: On: signing in takes a code.
admin.secondFactorOff: Off: the password alone opens the panel.
admin.secondFactorSetUpNote: Switching it on ends every other admin session.
admin.secondFactorLost: If the app is lost: set ADMIN_SECOND_FACTOR_RESET=true in the environment and restart the API. The panel then opens with the password alone.
admin.secondFactorOnNow: Two-step sign-in is on. Every other admin session was ended.
admin.secondFactorFailed: That did not work. Try again.
admin.accountFactorBody: For a holder who lost the authenticator app and the recovery codes: switch two-step sign-in off for the account. It then signs in with its password alone, and is told so by mail. Make sure the person who asks is the holder: afterwards whoever knows the password gets in.
admin.unreachableHint: The admin panel couldn't talk to the API. Check that the api container is healthy (docker logs diet-app-api) and that the web → api proxy is configured.
admin.generatedMissing: ingredients.generated.json is missing — only the hand-curated baseline will be seeded. Run npm run import:usda with an FDC_API_KEY first to add USDA whole foods.
admin.updateExplain: Wipes seed-origin recipes not referenced by any plan/favorite and any ingredient no recipe uses, then re-seeds from data/*.json. User profiles, plans, favorites and inventory are preserved.
admin.updatedSummary: Updated {when} · removed {recipes, number} recipes and {ingredients, number} ingredients that nothing used · hid {retiredRecipes, number} recipes and {retiredIngredients, number} ingredients that are still in use · now {newIngredients, number} ingredients / {newRecipes, number} recipes.

coverage.title: Recipes per diet and meal
coverage.explain: How many recipes a plan can choose from. With none, no plan can be made for that diet with that meal; with fewer than {enough}, a week repeats the same dish more often than a profile allows by default.
coverage.gap: {below, plural, =0 {Every diet has at least {target} recipes for every meal.} one {# of {pairs} pairs of diet and meal has fewer than {target} recipes.} other {# of {pairs} pairs of diet and meal have fewer than {target} recipes.}} A recipe run with "Fill what the catalogue lacks" writes for the emptiest pair first.
coverage.macrosExplain: What each diet aims at, and what a week's plan for it holds with the recipes there are, as percentages of a day's energy. A diet that is more than {points} points off needs recipes nearer its split: no setting brings a plan there.

usda.title: USDA importer
usda.explain: Pulls public-domain food data from the USDA FoodData Central API into data/ingredients.generated.json. Click "Update database" afterwards to load the new rows.
usda.demoKeyHint: Using the public demonstration key, which allows only a few requests an hour: enough for Foundation at most. Set FDC_API_KEY in .env, a free key of your own, for the larger SR Legacy import.
usda.doneSummary: Done. Wrote {kept, number} ingredients · {skipped, number} listed twice · excluded {excluded, number} by category.
usda.refusedSummary: {count, plural, one {# food was} other {# foods were}} left out: the source's record lacks a macronutrient, or its figures contradict each other. They are not stored as zero.
usda.overLimit: The food database takes no more requests for this key right now. Try again later, or set FDC_API_KEY in .env: a free key of your own allows far more.
usda.overLimitWait: The food database takes no more requests for this key right now. Try again in about {unit, select, hours {{count, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}} other {{count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}}}, or set FDC_API_KEY in .env: a free key of your own allows far more.
usda.keyRefused: The food database refused the key. Check FDC_API_KEY in .env, then restart the API.
usda.unavailable: The food database failed or did not answer. Nothing was changed; try again later.
usda.notWritable: The API cannot write to its data directory, so it asked nothing of the food database. In the stack built from source that directory is data/ in the repository: make it writable for the user the container runs as (chown 1000 data), then run the import again.

curation.explain: AI proposes friendly names for USDA ingredients; you approve, edit, or reject. Approved rows ship via PR.
curation.notConfigured: Set AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER and AI_DEFAULT_MODEL in .env to enable draft generation.

curation.userDraftHint: From users: its text and its slug can be changed. The ingredients are theirs.
curation.slugPrompt: The slug names the recipe in the data files: lower-case words and numbers joined by hyphens. Changing it does not send the draft back to review.
curation.promoteConfirm: Promote this user-drafted recipe into the curated library?
curation.pastReviews: {count, plural, one {# earlier decision} other {# earlier decisions}}
curation.pastApproved: {locale} approved by {label}{role, select, ADMIN { (administrator)} REVIEWER { (reviewer)} other {}}, {when}
curation.pastRejected: {locale} rejected by {label}{role, select, ADMIN { (administrator)} REVIEWER { (reviewer)} other {}}, {when}
curation.explainRecipes: AI drafts new recipes from the curated ingredient catalogue. You review, edit, and approve — nutrition is recomputed by the engine on every save.
curation.lastRunRecipes: Last run: wrote {written}, skipped {failed} · simple {simple} · medium {medium} · complex {complex}
curation.emptyRecipes: No recipe drafts yet — generate a batch above.
curation.nutritionStrip: {kcal, number} kcal · P {protein, number}g · F {fat, number}g · C {carbs, number}g
curation.fillCoverageHint: Each call writes for the diet and meal that have the fewest recipes, counting the drafts in the queue. The run stops when no diet is short of recipes for any meal.

runNotes.nothing-imported: Nothing to name: the catalogue has no imported ingredients.
runNotes.not-imported: {skipped, plural, one {Nothing to name: the ingredient given is not an imported one.} other {Nothing to name: none of the # ingredients given is an imported one.}} Only imported ingredients get their names from a run.
runNotes.all-have-drafts: {skipped, plural, one {Nothing to name: the one imported ingredient already has a draft.} other {Nothing to name: all # imported ingredients already have a draft.}}
runNotes.coverage-reached: Nothing to write: every diet has enough recipes for every meal, counting the drafts in the queue.

curation.rejectReasonHint: The validator rejected the model's output on every retry. Common causes: unknown-slug (model invented a slug), invalid-unit (used tbsp/cup), missing-field (skipped difficulty). Try a different model, or fewer recipes per batch.
curation.shipExplain: Local lands rows in this instance's DB (default). Upstream-PR opens a gh PR (admin only, off by default). Bundle downloads a JSON file you commit yourself.
curation.shipCurrentExplain: Exports the full ingredient-overrides.json as it stands now (every shipped override, rebuilt from the database) — independent of approved drafts, so it works even after you've shipped. Push opens a gh PR with the full file to the configured upstream repo.
curation.shipCurrentPushSuccess: Synced the current overrides — PR opened:
curation.shipPullExplainNoToken: Enter a public repo (owner/repo or owner/repo@branch) or the full address of the file. Pull fetches its data/ingredient-overrides.json and stores the names here as approved by people. Only public addresses are fetched from, unless the host is named in OVERRIDES_PULL_ALLOWED_HOSTS. For a private repo, set OVERRIDES_PULL_TOKEN (a GitHub PAT) in .env — the token is only ever sent to GitHub.
curation.shipPullExplainToken: Enter a public or private repo (owner/repo or owner/repo@branch) or the full address of the file. Pull fetches its data/ingredient-overrides.json and stores the names here as approved by people. Only public addresses are fetched from, unless the host is named in OVERRIDES_PULL_ALLOWED_HOSTS. A PAT is configured, so private GitHub repos work too.
curation.shipPullSuccess: Pulled {applied} of {total} override(s) into this instance.
curation.shipPullSkipped: Skipped {count} unknown slug(s) this instance has no ingredient for: {slugs}…
curation.shipPullRefused: {count, plural, one {# entry was refused because it breaks a rule for names:} other {# entries were refused because they break a rule for names:}}
curation.instanceDataExplain: Every recipe and name that ships into this instance is also copied to its data directory. To move to a new server, copy that directory over, update the database there, then restore: the recipes and names this instance added come back without the old database.

Whoever reaches the instance this way can claim any client address, and with it a fresh allowance for every limit. Close this way in (publish only the reverse proxy's port), or turn TRUST_PROXY off.
connection.overTrusted: TRUST_PROXY counts more proxies than wrote the X-Forwarded-For header of this request ({passed}). A visitor who writes that header themselves can then claim any client address, and with it a fresh allowance for every limit. Set TRUST_PROXY={passed}.

section1.title: What this is
section1.body:
Diet App is a self-hosted meal-planning application. The operator of this instance is responsible for its uptime, your data, and any service guarantees they choose to offer.

The software is Diet App by White Ravens, with its original source code at https://github.com/whiteravens20/diet-app. It is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3: anyone may share and change it on the terms of that licence, whose text is in the LICENSE file of the source code. It comes with no warranty of any kind. If this instance runs a changed version, the licence requires its operator to offer you the source code of that version.

section2.title: Accounts
section2.body: Creating an account requires an email address and a password you keep secret. You are responsible for keeping your credentials safe. Account deletion is permanent: when you delete your account the operator hard-deletes every row tied to it — profiles, meal plans, favourites, inventory, AI usage logs — with no recovery path.

section3.title: BYOK keys and admin AI mode
section3.body: When you enable BYOK ("bring your own key") in Settings you provide an API key for a third-party AI provider. The operator stores that key AES-encrypted at rest but does not insulate you from the provider's terms of service or pricing. When you use admin AI mode the operator is paying for your model calls within their configured monthly quota; abuse of that mode is grounds for the operator to disable your account.

section4.title: Nutrition is not medical advice
section4.body: Every calorie, macro and micronutrient value rendered by the application is computed by a deterministic engine from a curated ingredient database. Values are best-effort and not validated for any medical, clinical or therapeutic purpose. Consult a qualified professional before making dietary changes that affect a medical condition.

section5.title: AI-assisted content
section5.body: AI-drafted recipes, ingredient substitutions and meal swaps carry an ✨ AI-assisted chip. Review them before relying on them. The deterministic engine recomputes nutrition for every AI artefact and rejects nutrition the model invented, but ingredient choices and preparation steps remain AI-authored — sanity-check them against your own dietary needs and health.

section6.title: Curated content licence
section6.body: Curated recipes under data/recipes/ and curated ingredients under data/ingredients.json ship under the repository's licence, the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Recipes promoted from user contributions through the curation queue are contributed under the same licence by the act of submission.

section7.title: Data residency
section7.body: Your data lives in the database of the instance you are using. The upstream project has no access to it, no backups of it, and no recovery path for it. Ask the operator of this instance about backup policy and data handling before storing anything you cannot afford to lose.

section8.title: Liability and warranty
section8.body:
TL;DR: this is a free, open-source tool. Use your head.

The application is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, express or implied, including but not limited to the warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. In no event shall the operator of this instance, the upstream project, or any contributor be liable for any claim, damages or other liability — whether in an action of contract, tort or otherwise — arising from, out of or in connection with the application or the use or other dealings in the application.
